warnings.message: Excluded 2026-06-30 from sleep trends as it contains only 1.33 hours of sleep.
Recovery metrics are reported per their primary data source and are not merged across devices.
Daily activity trends come from activity summaries; workout types are counted separately.
Body composition trends are based on the most stable recent scale data source.

healthInsights.deepSleepAssessment: Device-estimated deep sleep is 23.05%. This is an algorithmic classification best used for personal long-term trends, not to determine recovery quality or a sleep disorder.
healthInsights.remSleepAssessment: Device-estimated REM sleep is 23.96%. This is an algorithmic classification; use your own long-term trend rather than inferring a cause from one proportion.
healthInsights.normalRangeAssessment: Recorded sleep averaged 7.14 hours over the last 30 days; whether that is sufficient depends on personal needs, daytime function, and the longer-term baseline; device-estimated deep sleep 23.05% and REM 23.96%; stage proportions are only used for personal trend observation; median bedtime 22:33; whether it fits depends on wake time, total sleep, regularity, and your schedule.
healthInsights.interpretation: Recorded sleep averaged 7.14 hours over the last 30 days; this report does not use one fixed range to decide whether it is right for an individual. Recent sleep duration remains stable compared to baseline, with no significant fluctuation.
actionableAdvice: Current sleep records are relatively stable. Continue a schedule that works for you and a comfortable sleep environment.
Aim for a reasonably consistent wake time that fits your life, including weekends; make changes gradually when needed.

notes: Sleep stage percentages are calculated based on the selected primary sleep data source only.

healthInsights.spo2Assessment: Recent device-recorded average SpO2 is 96.23%. A consumer-device reading cannot confirm lung function or rule out disease; the repeated trend is more useful than one reading.
healthInsights.normalRangeAssessment: Resting heart rate averaged 60.08 bpm over the last 30 days, +1.44 bpm versus the personal baseline; interpret it primarily through personal trends, symptoms, and measurement conditions; HRV average 47.56 ms - HRV varies greatly between individuals, so absolute values have limited reference value; trend changes are more important to monitor; Device-recorded SpO2 96.23%, within a common reference range; a consumer device is not diagnostic; Device-recorded respiratory rate averaged 15.88 breaths/min, +0.69 breaths/min versus the personal baseline; the export does not establish measurement context, so this report does not assign a universal resting category; VO2 Max 43.4 mL/kg/min; this report lacks reliable age- and sex-specific context, so it does not assign a high/low category.
healthInsights.interpretation: Recovery metrics are available; baseline data is still accumulating and trend assessments will become more reliable over time.
actionableAdvice: Current recovery metrics are relatively stable. Whether to maintain the current exercise plan should also depend on fatigue, pain, and training goals.
Measure at the same time each day (e.g., right after waking) to make trend comparisons more reliable.

notes: Recovery metrics are reported per their primary data source and are not merged across devices.

healthInsights.whoGuidelineAssessment: Apple Exercise Time extrapolates to about 140 min/week. This field does not fully establish intensity or unrecorded activity, so it cannot determine a gap to WHO guidance or generate an exercise prescription.
healthInsights.workoutVariety: Recent records contain multiple activity types (Walking;Traditional Strength Training;Running). Variety describes the mix; it does not by itself establish balanced training or lower injury risk.
healthInsights.normalRangeAssessment: Apple Exercise Time averages 20 min/day (about 140 min/week extrapolated); it supports personal trend review but is not the same as intensity-classified activity minutes; About 10.57 hours/day meet Apple's “Stand Hour” condition; this is not total time spent standing; Daily active energy 357.1 kcal.
healthInsights.interpretation: Apple Exercise Time can support personal activity trends but cannot determine compliance with public-health guidance on its own. Exercise volume remains stable — consistency is key to long-term benefits.
actionableAdvice: Recorded exercise rhythm is relatively stable; whether to maintain or change the mix should depend on goals, fatigue, and pain.
Continue recording workouts with the device or app you already use to follow personal trends; include activity type, intensity, fatigue, and pain when interpreting them.

notes: Daily activity trends come from activity summaries; workout types are counted separately.
Body composition trends are based on the most stable recent scale data source.
